recommendations.risk: cooperative progress/polling; D002 and decision D
recommendations.borrow: Shadow completed-call latency charging with deadline-aware rescheduling and a stored pending syscall result; Hermit epoll_pwait zero-timeout and blocking progress fixtures.
recommendations.scope: Source audit: Shadow feature defaults false; defaults are syscall cost 1000ns, vDSO cost 10ns, unapplied threshold 1000ns. The handler applies accumulated cost only when strictly greater than threshold, advances directly only within current event runahead, otherwise parks the already-completed result for resumption. The shim routes emulated RDTSC through clock_gettime. These are declared model costs, not measurements. A guest page whose clock stays constant between exits cannot rescue a kernel time-polling loop.
recommendations.constraints: A memory-only infinite loop still needs a supported intervention or explicit refusal. Shadow native timer preemption loses determinism and must not become a semantic control. Borrow integer cost parameters and deadline tests, not its entire threaded runtime or an implicit real-time model.

recommendations.borrow: rr PerfCounters_x86.h check_for_zen_speclockmap: event 0x510825 plus locked add; CPU-model-specific conditional branch selection from PerfCounters.cc; standalone counters-test as a diagnostic reference.
recommendations.scope: Current full rr identifies Zen3/Vermeer and uses raw event 0x5100d1 with PMU_SKID_UNBOUNDED. scripts/zen_workaround.py sets MSRC001_1020 bit54 across CPUs. The wiki documents loss over reboot/suspend and mitigation interactions; its script narrows MSR-reset interaction to Zen/Zen+, not generic proof for every Zen3 system. Even --check attempts modprobe msr when missing and can change per-process SSB mitigation.
recommendations.constraints: No script, modprobe, sysctl, MSR write or mitigation changes executed. counters-test/counters.cc excludes kernel and guest; it does not establish caller-read guest-only KVM counts. W5 must qualify its own guest-only counter and IRQ behavior. Fixed-branch pricing also cannot measure syscall-free branchless work, and overflow precision is separate from boundary-read repeatability.

recommendations.borrow: gVisor epoll_test, futex_test, mmap_test, sigaction_test/sigprocmask_test; LTP epoll_pwait01 and futex_wait01 as a small second oracle.
entrypoints: LTP checkout at pinned revision: make autotools; ./configure; make -C testcases/kernel/syscalls/epoll_pwait; ./testcases/kernel/syscalls/epoll_pwait/epoll_pwait01
LTP checkout at pinned revision: make -C testcases/kernel/syscalls/futex; ./testcases/kernel/syscalls/futex/futex_wait01
recommendations.scope: gVisor BUILD defines binaries and test/syscalls/BUILD generates native/runsc wrappers. Concrete tests include EpollTest.CloseFile, Oneshot, EdgeTriggered, UnblockWithSignal; SharedFutexTest.WakeInterprocessSharedAnon and WakeInterprocessFile; mmap covers sharing/COW/protection errors. LTP covers signal-mask/EINTR on epoll_pwait and futex timeout/wrong-value distinctions. Reuse binaries inside real Linux guest and compare with pinned native Linux where a reference is needed.
recommendations.constraints: gVisor and LTP suites were source-audited, not built. Shared shell lacks Bazel and LTP autotools. Guest staging must pin test binary plus needed loader/DSOs and record guest feature/configuration skips. No gVisor runsc is needed to test guest Linux. Full suites are not an initial acceptance gate. gVisor currently documents limited, default-disabled io_uring, so do not use its suite as proof for SQPOLL coverage. Passing conformance says nothing about fresh seeded equality.

recommendations.borrow: gVisor close/readiness and shared-futex/mmap cases; Reverie mechanism-versus-policy separation and typed ABI decoding as an architectural idea.
recommendations.constraints: No surveyed suite proves reboot incarnation handling or stale world completion rejection. Retain the world machine-ID/incarnation/request-ID tests from W1/W2. Current Reverie KVM is a bare identity-mapped Linux personality using host files, signals and worker cancellation, not a Linux guest kernel. Its standardized hypercall12 prototype ABI is explicitly unsuitable for a stock guest kernel. It must not replace the caller-owned runner.

recommendations.borrow: rr separation of counter consistency from observable output and replay diagnostics; DetTrace clock/stat/directory-order regression fixtures as leaks to detect.
recommendations.constraints: rr requires a recorded trace for replay; no recording is an O1 input. DetTrace and Hermit main tracers control selected userspace/kernel boundary effects, not autonomous guest Linux workers. None closes early-boot entropy, later kernel randomness, irq/device ordering or full KVM snapshot state. W3 remains the authoritative fresh-run witness rather than rr output equality.
